ArchitectureNotes.objective: Provide a GitHub-first, self-contained frontend task knowledge base that an AI agent can extend without catalog or graph drift.
ArchitectureNotes.non-goal: Do not build an executable learning platform, catalog generator, or mandatory repository runtime.
ArchitectureNotes.risk-1: Task metadata is canonical while the student catalog and knowledge graph are derived, so all three artifacts must change atomically.
ArchitectureNotes.risk-2: Structural verification cannot prove solution correctness; strict hybrid validation and mentor wave acceptance remain separate gates.
ArchitectureNotes.risk-3: Collapsed details prevent accidental spoilers but do not conceal solutions from raw Markdown or repository search.
ArchitectureNotes.risk-4: Publishing before deduplication can create several cards for the same learning goal.

contract.purpose: Store self-contained task cards whose metadata is canonical for every derived navigation artifact.

type-TaskMetadataSet.PURPOSE: Collection of canonical task metadata records exposed to the catalog

export-taskCard.PURPOSE: Expose the complete student-facing exercise through GitHub

notes.note-2: Collapsed solutions are spoiler-resistant, not access-controlled.

notes.note-4: Each accepted task adds one export-<task-slug> public annotation under M-TASK-LIBRARY in the knowledge graph.

contract.purpose: Provide the GitHub repository entry point and thematic, agent-synchronized projections of task metadata.

observability.critical-check: Every task appears exactly once and matches its canonical metadata.

notes.note-2: The catalog accepts an empty TaskMetadataSet so Phase 3 can create an explicit empty state before the first Phase 4 task wave.

DF-VALIDATE-TASK.NAME: ValidateTask
DF-VALIDATE-TASK.TRIGGER: Agent prepares a candidate for possible publication
DF-VALIDATE-TASK.step-1: The agent checks the learning goal against accepted tasks and merges semantically equivalent candidates.
DF-VALIDATE-TASK.step-2: The agent independently authors the candidate against M-TASK-TEMPLATE.
DF-VALIDATE-TASK.step-3: The agent applies identity, learning-value, contract, local-completeness, examples, solution, verification, and editorial gates.
DF-VALIDATE-TASK.step-4: The agent obtains task-appropriate temporary execution, type-check, trace, browser, or manual evidence.
DF-VALIDATE-TASK.step-5: The agent records accepted, needs-rewrite, rejected, or duplicate in Beads; only accepted yields an AcceptedTaskCard.
DF-VALIDATE-TASK.evidence: Validation decision, duplicate or rejection reason when applicable, evidence type, observed result, and unresolved risk.

DF-PUBLISH-TASK-WAVE.NAME: PublishTaskWave
DF-PUBLISH-TASK-WAVE.TRIGGER: Eight to ten accepted task cards are ready
DF-PUBLISH-TASK-WAVE.step-1: The agent creates accepted task cards and optional colocated assets.
DF-PUBLISH-TASK-WAVE.step-2: The agent synchronizes thematic README.md tables and one export-<task-slug> annotation per task.
DF-PUBLISH-TASK-WAVE.step-3: The agent runs V-M-TASK-LIBRARY, V-M-CATALOG, V-M-TASK-VALIDATION, and V-M-GOVERNANCE.
DF-PUBLISH-TASK-WAVE.step-4: The agent publishes a wave report containing decisions, evidence, merges, checks, and remaining risks.
DF-PUBLISH-TASK-WAVE.step-5: The mentor accepts the wave or requests fixes in the same story worktree and branch.
DF-PUBLISH-TASK-WAVE.step-6: The agent closes the child Beads issue only after mentor acceptance.
DF-PUBLISH-TASK-WAVE.evidence: Accepted paths, catalog rows, graph annotations, validation evidence, verification output, and mentor wave-acceptance status.

DF-ADD-TASK.NAME: AddTask
DF-ADD-TASK.TRIGGER: Mentor asks an AI agent to add a task
DF-ADD-TASK.step-1: The agent reads M-GOVERNANCE, M-TASK-TEMPLATE, and M-TASK-VALIDATION.
DF-ADD-TASK.step-2: The agent resolves mandatory metadata and environment and stops if classification is ambiguous.
DF-ADD-TASK.step-4: An accepted card follows the same atomic task, catalog, graph, and evidence contract as DF-PUBLISH-TASK-WAVE.
DF-ADD-TASK.step-5: The Beads issue remains open until mentor acceptance.
DF-ADD-TASK.evidence: Validation decision, task path, catalog row, graph entry, link results, hybrid evidence, and mentor-acceptance status.

DF-STUDY-TASK.NAME: StudyTask
DF-STUDY-TASK.TRIGGER: Student opens the repository on GitHub
DF-STUDY-TASK.step-1: The student chooses a task from README.md using visible metadata.
DF-STUDY-TASK.step-2: GitHub follows a relative link to the task card.
DF-STUDY-TASK.step-3: The student reads the visible goal, prompt, starter code, and readiness criteria.
DF-STUDY-TASK.step-4: The student optionally opens theory, targeted additional materials, and then reveals hints one at a time.
DF-STUDY-TASK.step-5: The student opens the solution after attempting the task and completes self-check questions.
DF-STUDY-TASK.evidence: Working relative link, matching metadata, visible required sections, and closed progressive-disclosure blocks.

DF-UPDATE-TASK.NAME: UpdateTask
DF-UPDATE-TASK.TRIGGER: Agent changes task content, metadata, path, prerequisites, or assets
DF-UPDATE-TASK.step-1: The agent treats the task card metadata and stable slug as the current canonical record.
DF-UPDATE-TASK.step-2: The agent updates the task content and identifies every derived artifact and inbound reference.
DF-UPDATE-TASK.step-3: The agent reruns every M-TASK-VALIDATION gate affected by the change.
DF-UPDATE-TASK.step-4: The agent synchronizes catalog placement and knowledge-graph facts.
DF-UPDATE-TASK.step-5: The agent checks uniqueness, metadata equality, prerequisites, assets, supplementary links, and relative links.
DF-UPDATE-TASK.step-6: A slug change uses a dedicated migration path and verifies all inbound references.
DF-UPDATE-TASK.evidence: Before/after metadata, validation evidence, unique thematic projection, resolved links, graph delta, and migration evidence when applicable.

Phase-1.name: Governance
Phase-1.goal: Record approved requirements, worktree isolation, technology boundaries, module contracts, data flows, verification references, and stop conditions.
Phase-1.step-1: Finalize and review the written specification and all GRACE planning artifacts.

Phase-2.name: TaskContract
Phase-2.goal: Create the canonical GitHub-first task structure and strict validation policy before any task content is added.
Phase-2.step-2: Create docs/task-validation-policy.md and prove all terminal decisions and hybrid evidence routes.

Phase-3.name: StudentEntryPoint
Phase-3.goal: Create an understandable repository landing page and an explicit empty catalog state.
Phase-3.step-1: Create README.md with navigation rules and the catalog projection contract.

Phase-4.name: CandidateAudit
Phase-4.goal: Freeze a finite neutral Beads candidate register, deduplicate it, and record a validation decision for every stable candidate ID.
Phase-4.step-1: Freeze candidate IDs, apply DF-VALIDATE-TASK, and group accepted cards into waves of 8-10 with a permitted final wave of 1-7.

Phase-5.name: TaskWaves
Phase-5.goal: Publish strictly accepted tasks through atomic task, catalog, graph, evidence, and mentor wave-acceptance updates.
Phase-5.step-1: Publish 8-10 accepted task cards from the canonical template, or 1-7 for the final incomplete wave.
Phase-5.step-2: Synchronize thematic student-catalog tables for the wave.
Phase-5.step-3: Apply graph and verification deltas and record mentor wave acceptance in Beads.

Phase-6.name: FinalAudit
Phase-6.goal: Prove that every candidate has a terminal decision and every accepted task remains unique, verified, linked, and mentor-accepted.
Phase-6.step-1: Run full candidate-status, catalog, graph, XML, Markdown, link, branch-divergence, and acceptance checks.

Phase-7.name: ScaleReview
Phase-7.goal: Reassess controlled vocabularies and deterministic validation only after observed catalog size or drift justifies added tooling.
Phase-7.step-1: Review drift evidence and explicitly approve or reject automation.

ExecutionPolicy.controller-owns: docs/development-plan.xml, docs/knowledge-graph.xml, docs/verification-plan.xml, and catalog synchronization decisions
ExecutionPolicy.worker-owns: Only the explicitly accepted task cards, colocated assets, and packet-scoped derived updates
ExecutionPolicy.replan-trigger: Ambiguous metadata or environment, duplicate learning goal, missing prerequisite or asset, unexpected GitHub rendering, contradictory task and catalog facts, unavailable mandatory evidence, or any requirement for new permanent runtime tooling.
ExecutionPolicy.checkpoint-requirement: Every step must leave assumptions, validation decisions, artifacts changed, checks run, observed evidence, mentor wave-acceptance status, and next action.
